name: MicroMeasuringGapTarget
quote: A very common type of gap occurs in any three consecutive trending bars on any chart. For example, if these three bars are trending up and the low of bar 3 is at or above the high of bar 1, there is a gap and it can act as a measuring gap or a breakaway gap.

name: LargeGapOpenFavorsTrendDay
quote: Large gap openings often lead to trend days in either direction.
description: Intraday filter: when the session's opening gap (open minus the prior session's close) exceeds a multiple of ATR, bias toward with-trend entries and treat the day as a likely trend day rather than a trading-range day.

complexity.reason: single session-open-vs-prior-close comparison against ATR; deciding which direction is 'the trend' is left to other filters

name: BodyGapBetweenBars
quote: Occasionally, there are gaps between the bodies (for example, the open of a bar might be above the close of the prior bar in a bull trend).
description: This bar's open trades beyond (above, in a bull trend) the prior bar's close -- a body gap, a strong sign of urgency.

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: MicroMeasuringGap
quote: if the low of the bar after a strong bull trend bar in a bull trend is at or above the high of the bar before the trend bar, this is a gap and a breakout test and a sign of strength.
description: Across three consecutive bars where the middle bar is a strong bull trend bar, the bar after it never trades back into the range of the bar before it -- a micro measuring gap and sign of strength.
pseudocode: close[1] > open[1] && (close[1] - open[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && low[0] >= high[2]

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar-offset arithmetic combining a bar classification with a gap test

chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: MeasuringGapHoldsBreakout
quote: Measuring gaps occur where the breakout test does not overlap the breakout point. For example, the pullback from a bull breakout does not drop below the high of the bar where the breakout occurred.
description: Since a designated breakout bar, no later pullback low has traded back below that breakout bar's high (bull case) -- confirms the breakout is holding and the trend is strong.

complexity.reason: requires first identifying and persisting a 'breakout bar' from an earlier, separately-defined breakout event, then tracking its high/low as state across all later bars

notes: 'Breakout bar' identification itself is out of scope for this candidate; assumed available as persisted state.
chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: BigGapOpen
quote: There is a big gap opening on the day. ... the 5 minute Emini gapped up 11 points, which is huge, and the first bar was a bull trend bar.
description: The session's opening price gaps beyond a threshold distance from the prior session's close -- a sign the day may become a strong trend day.

complexity.reason: needs session-boundary detection and the prior session's closing price carried as state

notes: gapThreshold is instrument-specific (points), Brooks's 11-point Emini example is not a stated rule value.
chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: GapDoesNotReverseEarly
quote: Large gaps that don't reverse early usually mark the start of a strong trend for the day and the day often closes at or near the high (or low, in a bear).
description: After a big gap up (T19-14), price has not traded back down through the prior session's close within the first N bars of the session -- confirms the gap is holding.

complexity.reason: window-low check combined with session state from T19-14

chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: GapOpenAsSpike
quote: Since any strong vertical move can function as a spike, a gap opening qualifies.
description: Filter/primitive: the session opened with a gap up of at least a multiple of ATR above the prior session's close (or high); treat it as a bull spike whose start is the prior close and end is the first bar's close, feeding the spike-and-channel candidates.
pseudocode: firstBarOfSession && open[0] - priorSessionClose >= gapAtr * atr  /* spikeStart = priorSessionClose, spikeEnd = close[0] */

complexity.reason: session boundary and prior-session close state

notes: Page 369: 'All down gaps are bear spikes and can be followed by bear channels.'

name: SmallOpeningRangeWithLargeGapTrendDay
quote: If this small range occurs when there is a large gap up, the odds of a trend day up or down are high.
description: Filter: a large opening gap combined with a small opening range - expect a trend day, take breakout entries and swing them.

complexity.reason: composes two session-state primitives

name: GapDirectionalBias
quote: When there is a large gap up and a trend from the open day forms, the day will be a bull trend day about 60 percent of the time and a bear trend day 40 percent of the time...The larger the gap, the more likely the day will be a trend day and the more likely the trend will be in the direction of the gap.
description: Soft filter: on a session that opens with a gap beyond a minimum size, prefer with-gap entries over against-gap entries (does not block the other side, just a bias weight/tie-break).
pseudocode: gapSize = open[0] - close[1]; abs(gapSize) >= minGapAtr * atr ? preferLongBias = (gapSize > 0) : preferLongBias = null
book_order_type: n/a (context bias, not a hard gate)

complexity.reason: single gap-size comparison, but 'bias' rather than a gate is a design decision for the authoring pass

notes: The 60/40 split itself is a base rate, not a per-bar test; recorded as a directional tilt candidate, not a hard block.
chapter_title: Trend from the Open and Small Pullback Trends

name: FirstBarBreakoutEntry
quote: If there is a gap open that is more than just a few ticks and the first bar is a strong trend bar (small tail, good-sized bar), trading its breakout in either direction is usually a good trade.
description: Entry: the session's first bar is a strong trend bar (large body relative to range, small tails) following a gap; buy the breakout of its high at the next open.
pseudocode: barsIntoSession == 1 && abs(open[0] - close[1]) >= minGapAtr * atr && bullTrendBar[0]  /* enter next open on a stop above high[0] */
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the first bar's high

complexity.reason: session-relative bar index plus a gap size and trend-bar test

notes: Page 419: 'Even if there is not a gap open, a trend bar for the first bar is a good setup for a trade' - the gap requirement can be dropped (minGapAtr = 0) for that variant.
